0018| ## Overview
0019| 
0020| The engine has no installer of its own. A user must assemble a runtime environment, make the engine reachable by hand, and there is no way for another program to learn which engine version a chosen target provides without actually installing it. Because of that, the companion client cannot be offered as a combined install and cannot decide whether an installed engine is usable. This task gives the engine a first-class per-user installer, a clean removal, and a non-destructive version answer that another installer can use before it decides anything.
0021| 
0022| **Outcome:** A user installs the engine with one action as themselves, gets a working engine in a newly started terminal session, can repeat that action safely and is told the installed version as one plain value; removal takes back exactly what the installer added and keeps user data; and a separate read-only mode answers which version a chosen target would provide, so the companion client's installer can compare it with an installed engine and install only a strictly newer one.
0023| 
0024| ## Product Intent
0025| 
0026| Forgel and Forgel Code must install and run as one working pair. Both must be installable by a non-expert on their own machine without administrator rights and without hand-editing start-up settings, and the pair must be installable together by one action. That is only possible when the engine's installer can answer 'which engine version would I get' without installing anything, and can install a chosen target reproducibly.
0027| 
0028| ## User Experience
0029| 
0030| The user copies one line into a terminal and ends up with a working engine, with no administrator prompt, no manual environment assembly and no hand-edited start-up configuration. Repeating the same line is safe and gives a newer engine when one exists. The last line of a successful install tells the user exactly which engine version is now installed. If something cannot be done — no supported runtime, unreachable source, or an older engine that would still win — the user gets a plain message naming the cause and the next action instead of a broken environment. A second, read-only mode answers 'which version would I get' without touching the machine, which is what makes the combined install trustworthy.

0111| ## Try the M0 Skeleton
0112| 
0113| Requires Python 3.11+.
0114| 
0115| The local console needs no Telegram bot, no token and no server:
0116| 
0117| ```bash
0118| make chat
0119| # forgel> /new My app | A minimal SaaS with a landing page and a health check
0120| # forgel> /status
0121| # forgel> /approve <project-id> staging
0122| ```
0123| 
0124| The console creates `.forgel-demo/`; the daemon runs the project through the
0125| pipeline to the staging gate.
0126| 
0127| For continuous work without a prompt, run the daemon in another terminal:
0128| 
0129| ```bash
0130| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel daemon --home .forgel-demo
0131| ```
0132| 
0133| The pipeline parks at the staging approval gate; nothing reaches `done`
0134| without a human decision:
0135| 
0136| ```bash
0137| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel list --home .forgel-demo
0138| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel status <project-id> --home .forgel-demo
0139| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel approve <project-id> --scope staging --home .forgel-demo
0140| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel run <project-id> --home .forgel-demo
0141| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel serve <project-id> --home .forgel-demo
0142| ```
0143| 
0144| Approvals are recorded in the ledger and in `docs/program/approvals.md` inside
0145| the project's control repository, together with the release the human reviewed.
0146| They are scoped to one generation, so a new generation asks again. Production
0147| approval is only accepted for a completed release and requires
0148| `--accept-compliance-responsibility`. For a multi-repository project the
0149| release is a digest of every repository state; the per-repository SHAs are in
0150| `docs/program/releases/g<generation>.json`.
0151| 
0152| **Autonomy vs gates.** The agent does not ask questions while it works. Before
0153| a release it decides reversible details itself, records every assumption and
0154| shows a finished result with evidence. It stops only for a material fork, an
0155| irreversible or production action, or missing access. The staging and
0156| production approvals are checkpoints on a finished result, not an
0157| interrogation; production data, payments and secrets stay human-gated.
0158| 
0159| **Context and handoff.** The runtime owns the context window. A long task runs
0160| in sessions; when the estimated prompt approaches the budget or a session
0161| hits its step cap, Forgel writes durable state to
0162| `docs/program/agent/<task>.state.md` and starts a new session from it. The
0163| model is told not to estimate tokens or ask to continue. The report shows the
0164| session count, handoffs and estimated usage. The window defaults to 1M tokens;
0165| tokens are counted with `tiktoken` when installed (`pip install
0166| 'forgel[tokens]'`, included in the Docker image) and with a conservative
0167| fallback otherwise. A task left `running` by a crash is requeued at the next
0168| daemon start and continues from its state file, up to three resumes. See
0169| `PLAN.md` §7.15.
0170| 
0171| **Task QA and milestones.** A task that the coding agent reports done is
0172| followed by an independent QA pass over the project's `environment.yaml`
0173| (`test`, then `e2e`) in the sandbox; a red gate fails the task with
0174| `docs/program/agent/<task>.qa.md`. The `e2e` command is the program gate, not
0175| another unit run: it tests the whole construction, and the planner refuses a
0176| project that needs it (interacting repositories, a frontend/acceptance or
0177| mobile repository, or sibling mounts) without one. The e2e suite
0178| lives in the project's main repository, or in the control repository for a
0179| project that started multi-repo; a red e2e returns to the coding agent with the
0180| command, workdir and output. A database or cache covered by the unit-test
0181| framework does not by itself require a program e2e; a browser, a mobile
0182| simulator/emulator or an external tool without a standard harness is covered by
0183| a real-interface command check in the task specification. A mobile simulator or
0184| emulator is deferrable: when it is absent on the current machine, the e2e step
0185| is `skipped` with instructions and the task is not blocked; heavy tools are
0186| declared in `e2e_requires`. A red environment
0187| `test` is a project failure, not
0188| a code defect, and does not spend a coder rework. `forgel plan` (or `/plan`)
0189| turns a
0190| milestone goal into an ordered backlog of task intents; a separate
0191| requirements writer expands each intent into a formal specification under
0192| `docs/program/specs/<task>.md`, and a plan review checks the whole set against
0193| the goal before queueing. `--dry-run` previews the specifications, and the
0194| daemon runs the plan's tasks in the order the plan lists them. The plan is committed
0195| as `docs/program/plans/<id>.md`. A free-text task that has no formal
0196| specification gets one, plus the external-dependency report, before the coder
0197| starts (`FORGEL_FREE_TEXT_SPEC=0` disables this). See `PLAN.md` §7.15.
0198| 
0199| **External dependencies.** While writing a specification, the requirements
0200| writer lists every external service, tool, binary, API or format the task
0201| touches. A separate dependency scout resolves each one before the task is
0202| queued: `direct` when a local or test interface is available (with evidence
0203| naming it), `stub` with documentation/source evidence and the stub code, or
0204| `unavailable` when no reliable source exists — which stops planning instead
0205| of guessing. The task record keeps the mode, the rendered specification
0206| carries the stub, the coder follows it, and the reviewer checks the stub code
0207| against the recorded evidence.
0208| 
0209| **Models and cost.** `deepseek-flash` is the default for every role; a more
0210| expensive model is an explicit configuration choice. Autonomous work defaults
0211| to DeepSeek's off-peak hours, when the rate is half the peak rate. During a
0212| peak window the daemon holds model-using work and free text answers with the
0213| window close time; `/peak` shows the schedule, `/peak always` and `/peak
0214| off_peak` set the policy, and `FORGEL_PEAK_HOURS` overrides the windows. See
0215| `PLAN.md` §7.16.
0216| 
0217| Run the tests:
0218| 
0219| ```bash
0220| make test
0221| ```
0222| 
0223| Run the core from the Docker image:
0224| 
0225| ```bash
0226| docker compose run --rm forgel init "My app" --brief "A minimal app."
0227| ```
0228|

0111| ## Try the M0 Skeleton
0112| 
0113| Requires Python 3.11+.
0114| 
0115| The local console needs no Telegram bot, no token and no server:
0116| 
0117| ```bash
0118| make chat
0119| # forgel> /new My app | A minimal SaaS with a landing page and a health check
0120| # forgel> /status
0121| # forgel> /approve <project-id> staging
0122| ```
0123| 
0124| The console creates `.forgel-demo/`; the daemon runs the project through the
0125| pipeline to the staging gate.
0126| 
0127| For continuous work without a prompt, run the daemon in another terminal:
0128| 
0129| ```bash
0130| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel daemon --home .forgel-demo
0131| ```
0132| 
0133| The pipeline parks at the staging approval gate; nothing reaches `done`
0134| without a human decision:
0135| 
0136| ```bash
0137| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel list --home .forgel-demo
0138| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel status <project-id> --home .forgel-demo
0139| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel approve <project-id> --scope staging --home .forgel-demo
0140| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel run <project-id> --home .forgel-demo
0141| PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m forgel serve <project-id> --home .forgel-demo
0142| ```
0143| 
0144| Approvals are recorded in the ledger and in `docs/program/approvals.md` inside
0145| the project's control repository, together with the release the human reviewed.
0146| They are scoped to one generation, so a new generation asks again. Production
0147| approval is only accepted for a completed release and requires
0148| `--accept-compliance-responsibility`. For a multi-repository project the
0149| release is a digest of every repository state; the per-repository SHAs are in
0150| `docs/program/releases/g<generation>.json`.
0151| 
0152| **Autonomy vs gates.** The agent does not ask questions while it works. Before
0153| a release it decides reversible details itself, records every assumption and
0154| shows a finished result with evidence. It stops only for a material fork, an
0155| irreversible or production action, or missing access. The staging and
0156| production approvals are checkpoints on a finished result, not an
0157| interrogation; production data, payments and secrets stay human-gated.
0158| 
0159| **Context and handoff.** The runtime owns the context window. A long task runs
0160| in sessions; when the estimated prompt approaches the budget or a session
0161| hits its step cap, Forgel writes durable state to
0162| `docs/program/agent/<task>.state.md` and starts a new session from it. The
0163| model is told not to estimate tokens or ask to continue. The report shows the
0164| session count, handoffs and estimated usage. The window defaults to 1M tokens;
0165| tokens are counted with `tiktoken` when installed (`pip install
0166| 'forgel[tokens]'`, included in the Docker image) and with a conservative
0167| fallback otherwise. A task left `running` by a crash is requeued at the next
0168| daemon start and continues from its state file, up to three resumes. See
0169| `PLAN.md` §7.15.
0170| 
0171| **Task QA and milestones.** A task that the coding agent reports done is
0172| followed by an independent QA pass over the project's `environment.yaml`
0173| (`test`, then `e2e`) in the sandbox; a red gate fails the task with
0174| `docs/program/agent/<task>.qa.md`. The `e2e` command is the program gate, not
0175| another unit run: it tests the whole construction, and the planner refuses a
0176| project that needs it (interacting repositories, a frontend/acceptance or
0177| mobile repository, or sibling mounts) without one. The e2e suite
0178| lives in the project's main repository, or in the control repository for a
0179| project that started multi-repo; a red e2e returns to the coding agent with the
0180| command, workdir and output. A database or cache covered by the unit-test
0181| framework does not by itself require a program e2e; a browser, a mobile
0182| simulator/emulator or an external tool without a standard harness is covered by
0183| a real-interface command check in the task specification. A mobile simulator or
0184| emulator is deferrable: when it is absent on the current machine, the e2e step
0185| is `skipped` with instructions and the task is not blocked; heavy tools are
0186| declared in `e2e_requires`. A red environment
0187| `test` is a project failure, not
0188| a code defect, and does not spend a coder rework. `forgel plan` (or `/plan`)
0189| turns a
0190| milestone goal into an ordered backlog of task intents; a separate
0191| requirements writer expands each intent into a formal specification under
0192| `docs/program/specs/<task>.md`, and a plan review checks the whole set against
0193| the goal before queueing. `--dry-run` previews the specifications, and the
0194| daemon runs the plan's tasks in the order the plan lists them. The plan is committed
0195| as `docs/program/plans/<id>.md`. A free-text task that has no formal
0196| specification gets one, plus the external-dependency report, before the coder
0197| starts (`FORGEL_FREE_TEXT_SPEC=0` disables this). See `PLAN.md` §7.15.
0198| 
0199| **External dependencies.** While writing a specification, the requirements
0200| writer lists every external service, tool, binary, API or format the task
0201| touches. A separate dependency scout resolves each one before the task is
0202| queued: `direct` when a local or test interface is available (with evidence
0203| naming it), `stub` with documentation/source evidence and the stub code, or
0204| `unavailable` when no reliable source exists — which stops planning instead
0205| of guessing. The task record keeps the mode, the rendered specification
0206| carries the stub, the coder follows it, and the reviewer checks the stub code
0207| against the recorded evidence.
0208| 
0209| **Models and cost.** `deepseek-flash` is the default for every role; a more
0210| expensive model is an explicit configuration choice. Autonomous work defaults
0211| to DeepSeek's off-peak hours, when the rate is half the peak rate. During a
0212| peak window the daemon holds model-using work and free text answers with the
0213| window close time; `/peak` shows the schedule, `/peak always` and `/peak
0214| off_peak` set the policy, and `FORGEL_PEAK_HOURS` overrides the windows. See
0215| `PLAN.md` §7.16.
0216|

0218| 
0219| ```bash
0220| make test
0221| ```
0222| 
0223| Run the core from the Docker image:
0224| 
0225| ```bash
0226| docker compose run --rm forgel init "My app" --brief "A minimal app."
0227| ```

0059| ## Scripted Client
0060| 
0061| Every operation of the local client is also a parameterized `forgel` subcommand
0062| that needs no interactive prompt. With `--json` a command writes exactly one
0063| JSON object to stdout and nothing else; without the flag the human-readable
0064| text is the output, unchanged from before.
0065| 
0066| ```text
0067| forgel say --project <id> --text "..." [--session <key>] [--json]
0068| forgel say "add a health endpoint" [--json]
0069| forgel status <id> [--json]
0070| forgel tasks <id> [--json]
0071| forgel task accept|reject|retry|cancel|add --project <id> [--task <id>] [--json]
0072| forgel plan <id> --goal "..." [--release-class minor] [--dry-run] [--json]
0073| forgel plan <id> --status [--json]
0074| forgel projects [--json]
0075| forgel session [<id>] [--session <key>] [--json]
0076| forgel use <id> [--session <key>] [--json]
0077| forgel history [--session <key>] [--limit N] [--json]
0078| forgel daemon [--once|--loop] [--interval S] [--max-cycles N] [--json]
0079| forgel pause [--json]
0080| forgel resume [--json]
0081| ```
0082| 
0083| The JSON envelope is flat and stable:
0084| 
0085| | field | meaning |
0086| |---|---|
0087| | `ok` | success flag |
0088| | `kind` | `answer`, `change_request`, `action`, `plan`, `status`, `tasks`, `task`, `projects`, `session`, `use`, `history`, `control` or `daemon` |
0089| | `text` | the reply text a human would see |
0090| | `error` | empty on success, a description otherwise |
0091| | payload | one operation-specific field: `task` (+ `task_id`), `tasks`, `plan`, `project`, `projects`, `history`, `paused` or `cycles` |
0092| 
0093| A failed call exits with a non-zero status and still writes one JSON object with
0094| `"ok": false` and the reason in `error`; the same reason goes to stderr. The
0095| payload never carries secrets.
0096| 
0097| `forgel say` is the single free-text entry point. It calls the same
0098| `CommandRouter` the console and Telegram use and reports what the message
0099| became — an `answer`, a `change_request` with the queued task id, a `plan` or a
0100| control `action` — together with the reply text. The CLI layer holds no second
0101| dispatch table.
0102| 
0103| The active project is a durable engine-side session, so the client keeps no
0104| state between calls. The session key defaults to `local` (the console's chat id
0105| 0) and is switched with `--session`: `forgel session <id>` and `forgel use <id>`
0106| set it, `forgel session` reads it back, `forgel projects` marks the selected one,
0107| and `forgel history` returns the recent conversation of the session as JSON.
0108| The full contract is in
0109| [docs/program/commands.md](docs/program/commands.md).
